children: Raw sugar futures on ICE rallied to a more than one-year high on Friday but later steadied as mills in top grower Brazil remain incentivised to ramp up sugar output.
New York cocoa hit a near 10-month high.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
was little changed at 18.22 cents per lb at 1202 GMT, having earlier hit its highest since April 2025 at 18.66.
* Excess rains have slowed the cane harvest in Brazil and there are more rains forecast for the world's largest sugar grower in the next two weeks.
* The rains, which are linked to the El Nino weather pattern, are bullish also because they reduce the amount of sucrose in the cane.
* Against that, however, depressed prices for cane-based ethanol in Brazil continue to tempt mills to ramp up sugar output at the expense of the biofuel.
* Less than a third of Brazil’s flex-fuel vehicles have used ethanol made from sugarcane so far this year, consultancy Datagro said.
* "Almost everyone we have spoken to over the last ten days is waiting for a retracement to begin," said physical sugar broker Deepcore.
* White sugar
was little changed at $524.60 a metric ton.
COCOA
* New York cocoa
rose 5.6% to $6,520 a ton, having hit a 10-month peak of $6,535.

* A delayed start to the harvest in top grower Ivory Coast could lead to port congestion as exporters are expected to rush to ship beans before EU rules banning deforestation-linked imports take effect at the year-end.
* London cocoa
rose 5.6% to £4,735 per metric ton.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
edged up 0.2% to $3.1430 per lb, having set a three-week low of $3.0645 on Thursday.
* Arabica coffee stocks on the ICE exchange hit a 26-year low on Friday as dealers scrambled for scarce supplies amid concerns the physical market will remain tight in the months ahead.
* Robusta coffee
rose 0.3% to $3,565 a ton.
